newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: INTERVIEW - Union Camp buys Argentine firm.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Union Camp buys Argentine firm.

text.p: Union Camp Corp has acquired Argentina's second largest flexible packaging firm in line with its strategy to expand in Latin America, Chairman and CEO Craig McClelland announced in an interview with Reuters.
He also said he saw most global paper product prices picking up towards the end of the year due to higher demand.
"As a U.S.-based corporation with a market position around the world we view Latin America as our main strategic growth opportunity," he said late Monday.

"We are specifically enthusiastic about Argentina," he added minutes before making a formal presentation on the purchase of a 75 percent stake in Argentina's Puntapel, whose flexible packaging products include bags for cement, flour and sugar.
He declined to disclose the value of the deal.

McClelland added the decision to buy Puntapel owed also to the success of the customs union Mercosur, formed by Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, adding the company was "continuing to study Brazil" and singled out Chile as another country that offers Union Camp great opportunities.

The purchase of Puntapel is the second of New Jersey-based Union Camp in Argentina after its 1994 acquisition of a 30 percent stake in corrugated packaging company Zucamor, which has annual revenues of about $65 million.

Puntapel ranks second in the domestic flexible packaging market with a 15 percent share after Chilean group CMPC which has about a 30 percent market share. Puntapel has annual revenues of about $14 million.

McClelland said he expected Union Camp's Argentine business to grow in the next three to four years to about $100 million, noting that, "In a country with virtually no inflation we think that is very significant."
Union Camp says it owns 1.5 million acres of woodland in the southeast of the United States.
McClelland said the firm was considering land purchases in Argentina.
The company invested in 1991 in a corrugated box plant in Chile. It also has plants in Ireland, Puerto Rico, Spain and Great Britain.
McClelland predicted world prices for most paper products would recover towards the end of the year due to a pickup in demand.
"I am encouraged we see a recovery underway ... I believe as we move into the latter part of the summer prices will start to move up because demand is holding up quite well.
"The reason for prices being soft is due to the capacity additions" in the sector, he said.
McClelland said Union Camp will post over $4 billion in revenue this year.
In 1996, the company earned a net profit of $85.308 million on $4.013 billion of revenues.
